images.title: Setting a first price you can test
images.alt: Five steps for pricing a digital product: define the outcome and alternatives, check comparable products, pick a price, sell, then test another price.
images.caption: The first price is a starting point. Total revenue across two tested prices decides whether it moves.

items.title: Name the outcome
items.text: What the buyer can do after using it, and what their other options cost

items.title: Check comparable products
items.text: Find five to ten that solve the same problem for the same kind of buyer

items.title: Pick a price in that range
items.text: Pricing well above the cluster means your page has to show why

items.title: Sell long enough
items.text: Wait until you have enough sales to trust the numbers

items.title: Try another price
items.text: Change only the price, run a similar period and compare total revenue

images.after: How to test a price honestly
images.title: Keep a price test fair
images.alt: Checklist for a fair price test: change only the price, match the period and traffic, record visitors, sales, revenue and refunds, ignore tiny samples.
images.caption: A small audience can need a few months per price before the difference means anything.

items: Change only the price between the two periods
Run each price for a similar period with similar traffic
Record visitors, sales, revenue and refunds for each period
Don't compare a launch week with a quiet week
Don't change the sales page or bonuses in the same week
Treat small gaps, like six sales against nine, as noise

images.title: Honest vs deceptive pricing
images.alt: Comparison of honest pricing tactics, like real former prices and stated launch deadlines, against inflated was-prices and resetting countdown timers.
images.caption: The FTC treats invented former prices and fake countdowns as deceptive. Real deadlines are fine.
images.note: General information about US guidance, not legal advice

columns.label: Honest
points: A was-price you really charged for a while
A launch price that ends on a stated date
Ending the offer when you said you would

columns.label: Deceptive
points: An inflated price set up to show a big cut
A countdown that resets when the page reloads
Urgency on an offer that isn't time-limited
